note: One client (cmd/s3bench/s3load, its own SigV4 signer) drove the OrFS-S3 gateway and MinIO, sequentially, inside one resource-capped container on the same machine. This receipt is data, not a leaderboard: rows are keyed by {system, mode, concurrency, object_bytes} and are never ranked across incomparable coordinates.
method: A PUT is one single-shot S3 PUT of a seeded object; a GET is one S3 GET of a pre-PUT object; mixed alternates. Latencies are exact observed samples (per-worker slices merged and sorted). Bounded windows; the driver's own sample buffer is capped.

workload.concurrency_note: the 4 KiB PUT arm and the get/mixed arms sweep 1 64 512; the 1 MiB PUT arm sweeps 1 64 because 512 concurrent 1 MiB bodies exceed the 2 GiB cap (the gateway buffers a whole PUT body)

OrFS-S3.gateway: in-process S3 over an append-only OrFS volume; no FUSE in the data path
OrFS-S3.group_commit: -group-commit (ORFS_GROUP_COMMIT=1); batch bound 128 transactions, max wait 2 (default) ms
OrFS-S3.put_transactions: one authoritative transaction per PUT (namespace.CreateFileData / ReplaceFileData), so a PUT takes one durability barrier

MinIO.availability_note: MinIO public images refuse access (docker.io/minio/minio and quay.io/minio/minio both answer with a registry access denial); no MinIO binary was obtainable, so no MinIO comparison was run
MinIO.note: client/server S3 server over its own local storage directory; the system most WORM is bought with today

not_comparable: durability: MinIO is a client/server object store with its own on-disk format and fsync policy; the OrFS-S3 gateway appends to an OrFS authoritative log. The two do not offer the same durability contract and their rates are not a like-for-like durability ranking.
data path: the gateway serves in-process from one local append-only volume; MinIO serves over its HTTP server from its own storage engine. Same client, same operations, different systems underneath.

batching is a property of the gateway's own authoritative log, not of the S3 protocol: the group_commit rows record, per PUT arm, the batch size that arm's live /metrics measured (transactions per durability barrier) and the PUT rate divided by the barriers taken. A single-machine, single-volume result; not comparable to MinIO's storage engine.

arms.note: scraped from the live gateway /metrics before and after the arm. barriers* is orfs_fsync_latency_seconds_count; put_commits_per_barrier is the PUT requests the arm completed divided by the durability barriers it took. The gateway commits a PUT as one authoritative transaction, so a value above 1 is the log group committer batching concurrent PUTs behind one barrier.
